I wrote the answer to `answer.json`. It lists five def-use pairs, and they are the same in all 10 tests. This comes from reading the code only; nothing was run.

**Why all 10 tests are the same:** every test builds a one-dimensional interpolant with a single `pybamm.Scalar` child and changes only the input value (0.1 to 1.0). So each call to `_function_evaluate` goes down the same path, `self.dimension == 1`, and returns at line 284. None of the 2D/3D code at lines 287–324 runs.

**The child's type:** `Scalar` stores its value as `np.float64` (`src/pybamm/expression_tree/scalar.py:57-60`). That type is not an `np.ndarray`, so the check at line 279 fails and the `else` branch at line 282 runs instead of line 280.

| variable | def_line | use_line | what happens |
|---|---|---|---|
| `child` | 278 | 279 | loop variable checked with `isinstance` |
| `child` | 278 | 282 | appended to the list as-is |
| `children_eval_flat` | 277 | 282 | `.append` reads the list |
| `children_eval_flat` | 277 | 284 | unpacked into `self.function(...)` |
| `evaluated_children` | 276 | 278 | parameter iterated by the loop |

The other tracked variables (`shapes`, `shape`, `new_evaluated_children`, `nans`, `nan_children`, `nan_eval`, `res`) exist only in the 2D/3D branch, so they never get a pair.
